Query OpenSearch as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__opensearch.R
oauth_db_opensearch_api.Rd

Search documents, run aggregations or use the SQL plugin with the visitor's current OAuth access token. Results retain OpenSearch's native JSON structure.

Usage

oauth_db_opensearch_api(
  authorization,
  url,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  timeout = 30,
  ca_bundle = NULL,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

auth$connection from a shinyOAuth server module, without parentheses. To select a saved authorization, pass a function that calls auth$connection(id).

url

HTTPS OpenSearch cluster base URL, including a proxy path if needed.

target

Token target name in the shinyOAuth client. NULL uses its default token, including for clients without named targets.

required_scopes

Additional permissions to check before use. Request consent and set the client's permission requirements in shinyOAuth.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

timeout

Maximum seconds for one HTTP operation, including a read retry.

ca_bundle

Optional path to a trusted CA certificate bundle.

session

Shiny session. Inferred when the helper is created in server().

Value

An R6 client with these methods:

  • $search(index = NULL, body = list(), query = list(), raw = FALSE) posts a Query DSL object to /<index>/_search. An index may be a name, pattern or character vector. NULL uses cluster-wide search.

  • $sql(sql, parameters = list(), raw = FALSE) posts SQL to /_plugins/_sql, returning its native JDBC-format JSON response. Parameters are an unnamed list of list(type = "integer", value = 30) descriptors for positional ? placeholders.

  • $request(path, method = "GET", query = list(), body = NULL, raw = FALSE) sends a native JSON request. Supply relative path segments, for example c("orders", "_doc", "42").

Details

Configure OpenSearch's Security plugin to accept your provider's JWT access tokens using OpenID Connect or JWT authentication. It must validate the issuer and audience and map the token's subject and backend roles to OpenSearch permissions. A Dashboards browser login alone is insufficient. This client uses bearer tokens, not AWS SigV4 or a shared service account.

Create the client in server(). Each operation obtains a current token, pins its authorization, and discards responses after account changes, sign-out or lost permissions. GET and HEAD retry once after HTTP 401. POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE are never replayed automatically, including searches and SQL queries. shinyOAuth renews tokens before requests.

JSON objects become named lists, arrays become lists, and large integers remain strings. Search hits, aggregations, totals and SQL schema metadata are preserved rather than flattened into a data frame. raw = TRUE returns an httr2 response. Searches that time out or report failed shards raise an error unless raw = TRUE; use $request() for filtered responses.

SQL requires the server's SQL plugin. There is no automatic pagination: search pages use native from/size or search_after in the body. Advanced SQL cursors and other JSON APIs are available through $request(); consume or close cursors before changing accounts. Bulk NDJSON requests are outside this client's JSON interface.

See also

vignette("opensearch", package = "shinyOAuthDB"). oauth_db_demo() runs a local OpenSearch and Keycloak example.

Other platform API clients: oauth_db_bigquery_api(), oauth_db_clickhouse_api(), oauth_db_cratedb_api(), oauth_db_databricks_api(), oauth_db_fabric_api(), oauth_db_libsql_api(), oauth_db_oracle_ords_api(), oauth_db_postgrest_api(), oauth_db_salesforce_api(), oauth_db_salesforce_data_cloud_api(), oauth_db_supabase_api()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
search <- oauth_db_opensearch_api(auth$connection,
  url = "https://search.example.org")
output$results <- shiny::renderPrint({
  search$search("orders", body = list(
    size = 20L, query = list(term = list(country = "NL"))
  ))$hits
})
} # }
